newsitem.title: CANADA: Barrick Gold silent as Aussie rumors swirl.
newsitem.headline: Barrick Gold silent as Aussie rumors swirl.

text.p: Canada's Barrick Gold Corp on Wednesday declined comment on persistent rumors that it was eyeing Australian gold miner Great Central Mines Ltd, while Canadian analysts said a foray into Australia would make strategic sense.
Great Central shares have jumped recently amid speculation that North America's biggest gold producer will soon launch a A$863 million bid for the Western Australian gold miner.
"Our policy is not to comment," Barrick spokesman Vince Borg said in a telephone interview on Wednesday.
Investment dealers at the annual Diggers and Dealers mine conference in Australia have speculated Barrick would launch a bid in the next few days.
But Great Central said in a statement on Wednesday that it has not received and is not aware of a takeover offer from Barrick.
Nevertheless, investors drove Great Central's stock up 0.10 to A$2.80 on the Australian Stock Exchange on Wednesday.
Barrick improved 0.30 to C$31.25 in moderate afternoon trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Wednesday.
Canadian mining analysts said share prices of junior gold producers are fairly cheap now and Great Central is an attractive target.
The low-cost producer mines the rich Bronzewing and Jundee gold deposits in the Yandal Belt zone of Western Australia.
It has proven and probable reserves of 4.87 million ounces.
"This would make sense for Barrick if they made a strategic decision to invest in Australia. Great Central tends to be a low-cost producer with respectable production," a Toronto-based analyst said.

Barrick has 10 producing mines in the United States, Canada and Chile, and two mines under development in Peru and Chile. The company has a production target of over three million ounces of gold in 1997.
Analysts said Barrick typically looks for an asset with good upside potential for reserves and production.
"They may seem as if they're paying quite high for something as in the case of Arequipa. But after equating what they paid to the ultimate reserves it becomes quite cheap," another analyst said.
Last year, Barrick acquired junior minerals explorer Arequipa Resources Ltd and its promising Pierina property for about US$800 million.
Barrick brought an initial 6.5 million ounces into reserves at Pierina and has identified a further 764,000 ounces of gold-mineralized material.
Australian media reports have suggested that Joe Gutnick, Great Central's largest shareholder, was willing to sell his 24.7 percent stake in the company.
But Gutnick said on Tuesday talk of a Barrick bid was "just speculation".
